content:
I don't have reliable introspective access to that. I can make rough estimates—I know some questions naturally invite short answers while others don't—but I can't actually "see" my response before generating it.

It's a bit like asking someone "how long will your explanation be?" They might guess "a couple sentences" or "probably a paragraph," but they can't know precisely until they've actually thought it through and spoken it.

I also can't easily predict mid-response how much more I'll write. I don't have a clear sense of my own token count as I go.

That said, I *could* choose to write short or long by design if you requested it ("answer in one sentence" vs. "give me a detailed explanation"). The constraint is real-time prediction of my own output, not the ability to follow length instructions.
